---
argmap-version: 0.3
title: "Source Quotes"
description: "Teaching example for the v0.3 quote line (>) from D59. A quote line carries a VERBATIM span of source material plus its [^locator] footnote, attached to the node above it, so the gloss can go back to being a claim a reader parses cold and the evidence sits beneath it where a renderer can see it. Four patterns: (1) the plain case, one supporting quote under a statement; (2) a stack of quotes on one node, which is what a post-D39 gloss used to look like inline, behind a convention no tool could see; (3) the ECHO pattern, where a verbatim fragment that is grammatically part of the gloss sentence stays inline in plain quotation marks and a > line carries the full sentence with its locator; (4) quotes on evidence lines, where the source states the inference rather than either end of it. Also shows an annotation comment, the per-file-free side-channel that parks a quote's translation. Quotes are never translated: the whole > line is byte-identical across a map's languages. The memo quoted below is invented for this example."
---

# The source for this map is an invented internal memo on chain-of-thought
# faithfulness, written for the example. Every quote below is illustrative,
# not a real quotation from any work.
#
# Three rules govern every quote line here: the text is verbatim, the line
# ends with its [^locator], and the line is exactly one line (the editor
# soft-wraps it; the format never does).

# 1. THE PLAIN CASE — claim in the gloss, its supporting quote underneath.
#    Order is advisory: gloss prose first, then quotes. The parser accepts
#    an interleaved block, the lint prefers this one, and the serializer
#    rewrites to it either way.

@faithful [Chain-of-thought text tracks the computation behind it] 0.4: the
  visible reasoning is the reasoning, not a story assembled afterwards
  > the stated reasons are a report, and reports can be written after the fact [^memo-ch2]

# 2. A STACK. Three fragments bearing on one claim. Before the > line these
#    lived inside the gloss, which is how a node stops reading as a claim and
#    starts reading as an evidence appendix.

@trained-to-please [Preference training rewards reasoning that reads well] 0.6:
  raters score whole transcripts, so transcripts drift toward what raters like
  > we rewarded the transcripts our raters preferred, and got more of them [^memo-ch4]
  > readability and correctness came apart in about a fifth of the sample [^memo-ch4]
  > no rater in the study reported checking a step they found persuasive [^memo-ch4]

# 3. THE ECHO. Here the source's phrase is a grammatical constituent of the
#    gloss sentence, so it stays in the gloss in plain quotation marks — the
#    node's own wording, borrowing the source's words — and the > line echoes
#    the full sentence with its locator so the provenance survives. In a
#    translated map the gloss fragment translates (it claims nothing about
#    being verbatim) while the > line stays in the source language.

@load-bearing [Edited steps change the answer often enough to matter] 0.7: the
  memo calls a step "load-bearing" when editing it moves the conclusion, and
  finds that most sampled steps are not
  > we called a step load-bearing when editing it moved the conclusion [^memo-ch3]

# 4. QUOTES ON EVIDENCE LINES — the source states the inference itself, not
#    the claim at either end of it, so the quote belongs on the $ line. The
#    #[de: ...] line above the first quote is an ANNOTATION COMMENT: an
#    ordinary comment to the parser, exempt from the translation byte-check
#    (unlike every other comment), and the reserved surface for real
#    attributes in a later version. Its tenant today is a parked translation.

$intervention [editing a step moves the answer] 0.6 @faithful | @load-bearing:
  causal dependence is the cheapest faithfulness test the memo could run at scale
  #[de: Ein Schritt, dessen Bearbeitung die Antwort aendert, war Teil der Rechnung]
  > a step whose edit changes the answer was part of the computation [^memo-ch3]

$rater-pressure [reward on readable reasoning selects for readability] 0.5 ~@faithful | @trained-to-please:
  what raters reward is what training delivers, whatever produced the answer
  > we optimised the transcript, and the transcript is what improved [^memo-ch4]

[^memo-ch2]: Invented for this example. A Memo on Reasoning Traces, ch. 2.
[^memo-ch3]: Invented for this example. A Memo on Reasoning Traces, ch. 3.
[^memo-ch4]: Invented for this example. A Memo on Reasoning Traces, ch. 4.
